problem: Given that ${\lambda }_{1}=-5+4\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{2}$ are eigenvalues of a real $2\times 2$ matrix $A$, find $\frac{2}{5}({\lambda }_{1}+{\lambda }_{2}).$

activity_context.topic_title: Finding Complex Eigenvalues of Real 2x2 Matrices

examples.knowledge_point: Finding a Complex Eigenvalue of a 2x2 Matrix Given Another Eigenvalue
examples.problem: Given that $\lambda_1=-2+3\textrm{i}$ and $\lambda_2$ are eigenvalues of a real $2 \times 2$ matrix $A,$ find $2(\lambda_1+\lambda_2).$
examples.worked_solution:
Since $\lambda_1=-2+3\textrm{i}$ is a complex eigenvalue of $A,$ the second eigenvalue of $A$ must be the complex conjugate of $\lambda_1.$
Therefore, 

$$
\lambda_2=\overline{\lambda}_1=-2-3\textrm{i}.
$$

Finally, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}2({\lambda }_{1}+{\lambda }_{2}) & =2(-2+3\text{i}+(-2-3\text{i})) \\  & =2(-4) \\  & =-8.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Compute the eigenvalues of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,A-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
A-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 1 \\ -2 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

Then, we compute the characteristic equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 1 \\ -2 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )(-1-\lambda )-1(-2) & =0 \\ -1-\lambda +\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}+2 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+1 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2} & =-1 \\ \lambda  & =\pm \text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are $\lambda =\pm \text{i}.$
